title: Expressions with sealed records
hints: A record pattern takes a record apart in the `case`: `case Add(Expr l, Expr r) -> eval(l, vars) + eval(r, vars);`. Patterns also work with `instanceof`: `l instanceof Num(double a)`.
In `simplify`, simplify both sides first and then look at the results: that is how `(1 + -1) * x` becomes `0 * x` and then `0`.
`vars` maps variable names to values (maps are covered in lesson 4.02): `vars.get(name)` gives the `Double` stored for that name, or `null` when there is none.

When a `case` needs several statements, give it a block and hand back its value with `yield`: `case Var v -> { Double value = vars.get(v.name()); if (value == null) throw ...; yield value; }`. For `show`, `d == (long) d` tells whether a `double` is a whole number, so `String.valueOf((long) d)` prints it without the `.0`.
